title: Body, Health & Nazar
tagline: Fevers, feelings, the evil eye, and turmeric milk for everything.
canDo: You can talk about how you feel, what hurts and what you can do

grammar.title: Feelings with 'mujhe … lagna'
grammar.body: Hunger, thirst, cold and liking happen to you: mujhe bhook lagi hai (I'm hungry), mujhe sardi lag rahi hai (I feel cold), mujhe achha lagta hai (I like it). The verb agrees with the feeling, not with you.

grammar.title: sakna (can)
grammar.body: Stem + sakta (m) / sakti (f) / sakte (pl/aap) + hoon/hai/hain. main bol sakta hoon = I can speak. Negative: main nahin bol sakta. Permission: kya main ja sakta hoon?

phrases.roman: aap ko kaisa lag raha hai?
phrases.urdu: آپ کو کیسا لگ رہا ہے؟

phrases.en: Someone's put the evil eye on you
phrases.note: Any illness, bad luck or broken phone after a compliment = nazar. Cure: Ammi waves red chillies around your head and burns them.

phrases.en: God has willed it (said with a compliment, to ward off nazar)

phrases.note: A greeting. Not an insult. (It's a bit of an insult.)

phrases.roman: tum kitne patle ho gaye ho!
phrases.urdu: تم کتنے پتلے ہو گئے ہو!
phrases.note: Said by the same aunty, to the same person, one year later.

phrases.roman: Kya hua? Chehra utra hua hai
phrases.urdu: کیا ہوا؟ چہرہ اترا ہوا ہے
phrases.en: What's wrong? Your face looks drained
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Mere sar mein bohat dard hai
phrases.urdu: میرے سر میں بہت درد ہے

phrases.roman: Nazar lag gayi hai! Kal Mrs. Butt ne tumhari tareef ki thi
phrases.urdu: نظر لگ گئی ہے! کل مسز بٹ نے تمہاری تعریف کی تھی
phrases.en: It's nazar! Mrs. Butt complimented you yesterday
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Ammi, yeh nazar nahin, virus hai
phrases.urdu: امی، یہ نظر نہیں، وائرس ہے
phrases.en: Mum, it's not nazar, it's a virus

phrases.roman: Chalo, pehle mirchein waarti hoon. Phir haldi wala doodh
phrases.urdu: چلو، پہلے مرچیں وارتی ہوں۔ پھر ہلدی والا دودھ
phrases.en: Right, first I'll do the chillies. Then turmeric milk
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Virus bhi nazar se hi aata hai. Haldi wala doodh piyo
phrases.urdu: وائرس بھی نظر سے ہی آتا ہے۔ ہلدی والا دودھ پیو
phrases.en: Viruses come from nazar too. Drink your turmeric milk
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Main Bilal ko phone karti hoon. Woh doctor hai
phrases.urdu: میں بلال کو فون کرتی ہوں۔ وہ ڈاکٹر ہے
phrases.en: I'm calling Bilal. He's a doctor
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Bilal keh raha hai: aaram karo, paani piyo
phrases.urdu: بلال کہہ رہا ہے: آرام کرو، پانی پیو
phrases.speaker: ammi

phrases.roman: Ji Ammi, main theek ho jaunga
phrases.urdu: جی امی، میں ٹھیک ہو جاؤں گا

phrases.roman: Main ne bhi yahi kaha tha!
phrases.urdu: میں نے بھی یہی کہا تھا!
accept: main ne bhi yahi kaha tha

phrases.roman: Mashallah, mera bachcha. Ab aaram karo
phrases.urdu: ماشاء اللہ، میرا بچہ۔ اب آرام کرو
phrases.speaker: ammi

lessons.title: Main beemar hoon
lessons.blurb: Say what hurts. (Ammi will diagnose nazar anyway.)
lessons.canDo: You can say you're ill and describe what hurts

teach.title: Pain lives IN things
teach.info: 'I have a headache' is 'mere sar mein dard hai': there is pain in my head. Swap the body part: pait (stomach), kamar (back), daant (tooth).

exercises.prompt: Your head is pounding. Tell Ammi.

lessons.title: Bhook lagi hai
lessons.blurb: Hungry, thirsty, cold, sleepy: feelings happen TO you in Urdu.
lessons.canDo: You can say you're hungry, thirsty, tired, sleepy or cold

teach.title: Feelings 'strike' you
teach.info: In Urdu you don't 'be' hungry, hunger strikes you: mujhe bhook lagi hai. Same with thirst (pyaas), cold (sardi), and liking (achha lagna).

lessons.title: Nazar & haldi
lessons.blurb: The desi medical system: evil eye, turmeric milk, and Mashallah.
lessons.canDo: You can talk about nazar and desi remedies (and say Mashallah)

teach.tip: Compliment a baby without Mashallah and watch the room go silent.

exercises.prompt: You compliment your cousin's new baby. What MUST you add?

options.feedback: Inshallah is for the future. Mashallah is for praise.
Thanking the baby? Sweet, but no.

exercises.prompt: Ammi asks how you're feeling. You're better.
Type the word that protects a compliment

lessons.title: Sakna: can
lessons.blurb: Can, can't, may I. Plus the aunty weight report.
lessons.canDo: You can say what you can and can't do, and ask permission

teach.title: sakna = can
teach.info: Verb stem + sakta/sakti/sakte + hoon/hai/hain. Bol (speak): main bol sakta hoon. Add nahin for can't: main nahin kha sakta. Turn it into permission with kya at the start.

teach.tip: A useful lie at any dawat.

exercises.prompt: You're a woman. Tell Khala you can speak Urdu now.
An aunty says “Tum mote ho gaye ho!” What's the polite response?

options.text: Smile and say “Ji Aunty, aap ki duaaein”
Point out that she has too
options.feedback: True, but you'll never be invited again.

exercises.prompt: You're a guy. Type: “I can speak Urdu”
You're a guy at a dawat: “I can't eat any more”

boss.title: Ammi, MD
boss.blurb: You're sick. Ammi has a diagnosis (nazar), a treatment plan (turmeric), and a second opinion (Bilal).
boss.scene: You're on the sofa under three blankets. Ammi walks in, takes one look at you, and puts down her shopping. A full desi medical consultation is about to begin.
boss.canDo: You can explain how you feel and get through a desi home treatment

options.reaction: Science vs Ammi. You know who wins.
Wise. Never argue with the doctor.

f.prompt: The turmeric milk is coming. Accept your fate?

options.reaction: She heard 'I love turmeric'. Two glasses.
Correct, and yet nobody will remember you said it.

end.title: Treatment complete
end.text: You described your symptoms, survived the nazar diagnosis, and drank the turmeric milk. You'll be better by morning. Ammi will credit the chillies.
